title: Item Search — Products: Prep/Return date-time values overflow their field box for most months (AM/PM renders past the border)
requirementSource: NM-2253 'Automate Item Search' (office 1101 scope). The Phase-0 Jira sweep (jira-defect-crossref-item-search-2026-08-31.md — full NM-4 child read, 193 tickets) has no ticket describing the date trigger's fixed width or sanctioning clipped values, so no by-design reclassification applies.
stepsToReproduce: Open Item Search -> Products for office 1101 (cloudapps-e2e).
Open the Prep date popover and use the calendar's next-month arrow to reach a long-named month (e.g. November), pick the 22nd, close the popover.
Look at the Prep field: the value ('Nov 22nd, 2026, 12:00 AM' style) runs past the right edge of the field box — the AM/PM tail sits outside the border.

Repeat across all 12 months (probe cycled Oct 2026 through Sep 2027): 7 of 12 overflow on Prep — Oct +12px, Nov +27px, Dec +27px, Jan +11px, Feb +17px, Aug +5px, Sep +30px; Mar–Jul fit. The Return field shows the same class (+23px measured at November).
expectedBehavior: The selected date-time value renders fully inside the field box in every month — by widening the trigger, shortening the format, or truncating with an ellipsis inside the border.
actualBehavior: For 7 of 12 months on Prep (and on Return), the rendered value is wider than the trigger box and the tail (the AM/PM part) paints outside the field border, visibly spilling into the surrounding panel.

mcpEvidence.findings: Month-cycling probe on cloudapps-e2e office 1101: for each month the probe picked the 22nd and measured the trigger's scrollWidth minus clientWidth. Prep overflows in 7 of 12 months (+5px to +30px; Mar–Jul fit because their names are short); Return measured +23px at November. Screenshot .playwright-cli/page-2026-09-01T10-59-30-124Z.png shows both fields with the AM/PM tail outside the box border. Per-month pixel table recorded in specs_planning/_internal/field-inventories/item-search-product-search-2026-08-31.md (Prep/Return rows, DEFECT 2026-09-01 notes).

baselineEvidence: Old-site walk environment-blocked: navigator2.training.psav.com rejects automated-browser TLS ClientHello (curl/schannel gets 200; Playwright Chromium/Edge refused) — 6 retries, recorded in specs_planning/_internal/old-site-baseline/item-search-2026-08-31.md. The legacy page also predates this date-trigger widget, so no regression claim is made.
networkEvidence: n/a — pure client-side rendering defect; no request is involved in painting the field value.

verificationLog.detail: TC-ISR-PRS-021 automates the 12-month cycle on Prep plus a Return sample and pins this defect as an expected failure (the suite reports it as a known defect and will flag 'passed unexpectedly' the day the rendering is fixed). The run ends with Reset so nothing persists. Initial single-month reads had missed this: only the September default was ever rendered, and September happens to overflow by just +11px on a settled read — the month-cycling probe was added at the owner's request and surfaced the full pattern.
verificationLog.minimalRepro: Prep popover -> next month -> pick the 22nd -> close -> compare value width vs box.

verificationLog.detail: Re-measured live on cloudapps-e2e office 1101 by the same method as the 2026-09-01 probe (trigger scrollWidth minus clientWidth, plus the computed box). The application now renders the month ABBREVIATED rather than in full: Prep reads 'Nov 22nd, 2026 12:00 AM' at 205.1 px of text inside a 232 px content box, Return reads 'Dec 22nd, 2026 11:59 PM' at 200.6 px — spill 0 on both, with overflow-x hidden on the trigger. The 2026-09-01 evidence quotes the same field as 'November 22nd, 2026 11:59 PM', so the format itself changed; the shorter string is what now fits. A viewport difference was ruled out first: the 2026-09-01 screenshot is 1920x1080, the same viewport the runner uses. TC-ISR-PRS-021 has had its expected-fail pin removed and now passes green as a live regression guard (solo run 2026-09-03, 9.6s, no teardown error) — the field clips its own overflow, so a return to the longer format would surface here immediately as spill. STATUS LEFT AT 'open' DELIBERATELY: this file records the measured fact, but closing or withdrawing the filing is the owner's triage call, and this repository has no 'fixed' status value in use (only open / invalid / withdrawn).

notes: Rendering/layout defect (value paints outside its container) — a behaviour-of-the-pixels finding, not a markup/accessibility finding, so it is fileable for this client. Related but distinct: the pair validation (Prep > Return -> inline error + disabled Search) works correctly and is covered green by TC-ISR-PRS-020.
